speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are presenting with gait and limb ataxia; to begin my assessment, can you describe exactly how your walking and coordination have changed, and for how long have you noticed these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for describing that; the "drunken" appearance and right-sided clumsiness suggest a cerebellar issue. To narrow this down, can you tell me if anyone has noticed any changes in your speech, such as slurring or a scanning quality, and whether you experience double vision or drooping eyelids?

speaker: Patient
text:
I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI results indicate multifocal demyelinating lesions without enhancement, consistent with Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML), likely due to natalizumab therapy. Given your history of Crohn's disease and current symptoms, this is a known adverse effect of your medication. Did you experience any recent cognitive changes, such as memory loss or confusion, alongside your gait issues?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had a recent fever or major infection that I know of. The symptoms are mostly gait imbalance, limb ataxia, and weaker use of my right arm.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML).

The MRI findings of non-enhancing multifocal demyelinating lesions in the context of natalizumab therapy are diagnostic. The lack of fever or infection supports an opportunistic viral etiology rather than an acute inflammatory event.
